currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### FL-03 — One clock, work and rest The campaign uses one elapsed clock. A Watch is eight hours; a day contains Morning, Afternoon and Evening Watches. Combat rounds, rests, travel, treatment and work occupy their actual time within that clock. Completing a task does not add a second Watch. Entering Haven, changing teams or starting initiative does not reset elapsed time. A generic Watch task needs **480 active minutes** before its completion check. Feasible unfinished work can continue in another Watch, without a proportional completion reward. Exact recipes, uninterrupted training, treatment, rest and spells keep their own interruption rules. Guarding, travelling, casting, directing, interpreting, assisting or working cannot also count as incompatible rest. Passive carriage qualifies for rest only when a genuinely suitable safe berth and the actual rest requirements are satisfied. Plan at most two active work Watches and one Rest Watch per person each day. Evening is the default Rest slot; change it prospectively before that day's first assignment. Voluntary extra noncrafting travel or guard duty can replace Rest and incur its real costs and Rest Debt. This supplies no third crafting, training, research or harvesting Watch. Emergencies still consume time and interrupt the activity underway. Missing a scheduled Rest creates **Rest Debt**. If an emergency interrupts Rest, the debt opens after that emergency ends; otherwise it opens when the missed Rest Watch ends. Complete a qualifying safe eight-hour Rest by the end of the second following canonical Watch. If the debt remains unpaid at that deadline, gain 1 Strain once for that due event and keep owing the Rest. Missing another scheduled Rest while indebted gives 1 Strain and resets the deadline. There is no automatic additional Strain every second or every Watch merely because the same debt remains. A safe eight-hour Rest clears the debt even when you cannot receive another Long Rest's benefits. Keep the separate limits: one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours, two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests, the existing four-hour Morale Rest, and 24-hour Haven care. Trance reduces sleep, not the eight-hour Long-Rest requirement. Use the actual Strain and recovery chapter for what can be removed.

### FL-04 — Supply and daily support **Supply is a basket of real goods:** 2 lb of ration-equivalent edible food, 8 pints of potable water, 1 pint of compatible lamp oil in its flask, and 0.25 lb of ordinary camp sundries. The food and water cover one Small or Medium character's daily demand; Large characters require twice those quantities. This is game accounting. Two pounds of food equal three reviewed Cooking servings; a Large food day is six servings. Track food and water actually consumed, by recipient and lot. Ordinary partial rations credit their edible mass. A fractional magical meal never gives a fractional benefit unless its own source permits that. The same serving cannot be spent in a recipe and remain available to eat. Oil and sundries are spent when actually used. Do not burn spare oil or throw away sound stock to satisfy an abstract daily debit. The source lamp burns one pint in six hours. One actual light may serve several people within its real illumination, with its fuel spent once. A sufficient daylight or other safe lighting plan can use no oil; extra darkness, heating or work needs its real equipment and fuel. At each canonical 24-hour day endpoint, settle each recipient's actual food, water and necessary declared logistics support. A recipient short of any requirement gains **1 expedition Strain total for that day's shortfall**. Missing food and water does not give two Strain. Retain partial consumption credit. The unsupported day blocks Strain removal; that block can clear on a later day only with a real sufficient provisioning plan available and maintained. Crossing a gate does not erase needs: actual Haven/home support pays needs outside the expedition. Allocate shortages before the deadline. Joining, leaving or changing size/form divides demand by actual time and diet; it never refunds goods already consumed. A diet exception removes only its stated obligation. It gives no transferable provisions, fuel or camp labor. Unsupported nonmount Tiny, Huge or Gargantuan diets require their real profiles; mounts use their separate profiles. If an exact procedure charges **one whole Supply**, reserve and commit the entire physical basket, or a substitute that procedure actually permits. Wound treatment keeps its one-Supply cost at the start, even if treatment fails or is interrupted. Food or water genuinely consumed by its named patient or healer can credit that person's daily need once. The committed basket does not also remain in inventory or feed another person.

A recipient consumes two different cooks' portions before resting: there is one +1 entitlement, one fixed one-hour deadline from the first qualifying portion, and no +2 or timer refresh. A poisoned ingredient remains poisoned.

completePreservedProposalRecord.procedure: NEW finite search procedure: choose an accessible previously occupied site and spend thirty active minutes searching one bounded area, such as a room, wreck compartment or campsite. Before the roll the Director records the actual recoverable mundane equipment/supplies, their condition, ownership and access barriers. The die cannot create missing lots: take no more than actually exist and are within those limits. The player chooses which identified lots to retrieve, paying any separate safe-access/removal time; uncollected objects remain in place. These are ordinary catalog-compatible items or usable supplies, not magic loot, a free recipe ingredient classification or converted gp-to-Supply. A larger valuable object can be noticed by the normal search result but is not granted as an extra feat output. Mark searched evidence and removed quantities; another unchanged search of the same area gives no fresh roll or generated inventory. Genuine new access, deposited material or a different bounded area can justify a new attempt.

A found locked chest still requires opening and ownership consequences. Repeating the scavenging roll cannot turn its unknown contents into free mundane supplies.

### FL-06 — Foraging a finite place A generic Forage attempt requires 480 active minutes, suitable gathering implements and access to a real opportunity. The lead makes WIS (Survival) against the route-tier DC; up to three trained assistants can provide meaningful +1 help unless an exact source changes that procedure. The opportunity has an ordinary Sustenance allowance S from 0 to 4 and actual food, water and material quantities. Sustenance 0 gives no routine award. Success can recover up to S provision-equivalent units. Critical Success can recover up to **S + ceil(S/2)**, but the extra must come from an existing recorded reserve. A good roll cannot supply absent water, lamp oil, animals, herbs or industrial sundries. Receive the actual gathered goods. A food-only site supplies food, not a complete basket. A complete Supply requires every component to exist and its real gathering/packing work to be completed. The recovered amount cannot exceed the site's real remaining allowance and matter. Teams using the same opportunity share its allowance. Use one lead/check or genuinely disjoint portions allocated in advance, with no more total stock than the parent site contains. A new Watch, renamed site, new container or return visit does not replenish the place. Record gathered, ruined, inaccessible, forfeited and remaining quantities. Failure gives nothing and ends that attempt; an unchanged immediate retry is unavailable. On Critical Failure, contaminate one actual selected ordinary provision unit only when a predeclared contamination hazard supports it; otherwise add 1 Pressure once for that cause. An actual class/background permission to gather during a beneficial Long Rest supplies only its named product and real components. It does not also complete generic Forage or create a second local pool.

currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### FL-19 — Arriving at Haven Use this order for a full return: **inspection/quarantine → provenance → appraisal → claims/liens → disposition → settlement → recovery → standing → advancement → next descent**. A Tier-I return may use inspection → appraisal → sale → sponsor settlement → recovery only when every arriving lot qualifies and there is no disputed ownership, strategic cargo, lien, quarantine issue, contraband or faction hearing. The shorter route removes redundant administrative passes. It does not waive taxes, title, actual fees, care, unknown hazards or later standing/advancement records. A discovered disqualifier moves the same return to the full process, keeping work and charges already completed. | Ordinary work | Active time and unit | |---|---| | Intake | 10 minutes per arriving Expedition, with receiving officer and representative | | Additional flagged-lot inspection | 10 minutes per distinct homogeneous lot/assembly | | Provenance, including an uncontested claim check | 30 minutes per title/evidence dossier | | Appraisal | 30 minutes per item or previously constituted homogeneous lot | | Ordinary disputed-claim hearing | 2 hours with actual parties, evidence and authorized adjudicator | | Buyer negotiation/disposition | 30 minutes per coherent offered bill | | Ledger/sponsor settlement | 30 minutes per Expedition bill | | Standing notification | 10 minutes when needed | | Advancement record | 10 minutes when needed | | Next-charter planning | 60 minutes | Real waiting for staff, evidence or authority adds elapsed time. Independently staffed desks can work on separate lots, but one representative cannot fully participate in incompatible simultaneous tasks. Handing over a completed document uses actual handling time rather than automatically repeating its full review. Exact specialist, identification, emergency or hearing procedures keep their own requirements. Routine intake and uncontested bookkeeping need no roll. For uncertain appraisal, declare the appropriate INT skill—Arcana, History, Nature, Religion, Engineering or Investigation—or applicable craft tool and method. Add one proficiency where actually applicable; ordinary appraisal has no universal trained-only gate. Use the item's assessment DC, or its actual material-tier DC: I 12, II 13, III 15, IV 16, V 18, VI 19. One knowledgeable helper can provide ordinary Help under the social procedure; do not also add the generic expedition +3. Success gives reliable conclusions supported by that method/evidence and a valuation in the correct domain. A critical adds the declared extra supported detail or access to a real alternative buyer. Failure leaves only established broad facts and unresolved value. A predeclared critical-failure stake can produce a fallible report, never change the object's real identity. Testing consumes a sample only when declared and actually debited. Rotating appraisers over unchanged evidence does not create fresh checks. Identification, translation, title evidence, safe containment and a buyer's offer are distinct. Quarantine records an authorized institution's actual custody/location/access restriction; it neither destroys nor cleanses the item. Paid secure storage cannot substitute for an active core's specific containment.

### FL-20 — Choose one valuation method Before pricing, identify the actual offered object and quantity, condition, custody, lawful disposition and buyer. Choose one domain: ordinary equipment, reviewed crafted item, ordinary material/trade lot, true artifact, or an unsupported/unvalued object. A grand name, rarity label, high price, ingredient or magical condition does not choose the domain. **Ordinary equipment.** Use its actual grade/size/fitting baseline and the reviewed buyer rules. For an undamaged mundane item to which that schedule applies, the buyer's actual Honored/Liked/Neutral/Disliked/Hated relationship gives 75/60/50/40/25% of baseline; refusal remains possible. Damaged goods need a real condition-specific quote. Gems, jewelry, art and trade goods keep their particular transaction rules. Do not apply an additional Loop multiplier to an already calculated equipment price. These percentages are not magical-item buyback. **Reviewed crafted items.** Use their exact recipe reference and sale restrictions. For the reviewed durable supplemental-body families, use the actual source-batch/Standard-Q plus approved body reference once. Final quality yield, a legacy price, all reusable capital or artifact quality do not replace that reference. Charges, flaw, damage and permitted disposition affect the actual item's quote, without an automatic scrap floor. Retained catalysts and unused output reserves remain separate real stock. **Ordinary nonartifact, nonequipment material/trade lots.** Where no overriding exact quote applies, use: `Base × Provenance × Demand × Condition × Urgency` Base is that lot's actual source reference. If genuinely absent, the Director can establish one finite homogeneous lot using these explicit new provisional references before the offer: | Source band | Preserved lot range | New median reference | |---|---:|---:| | I | 5–15 gp | 10 gp | | II | 15–50 gp | 30 gp | | III | 51–148 gp | 100 gp | | IV | 151–499 gp | 320 gp | | V | 512–1,465 gp | 950 gp | There is no general Tier-VI-or-higher median. These are finite lot values, not per-pound prices or values renewed by splitting a lot. | Factor | Applicable values | |---|---| | Provenance | Undocumented 0.5; disputed 0.75; documented 1; actual Gate-Sealed 1.25 | | Demand | Glut 0.75; normal 1; sought 1.25; strategic 1.5 | | Condition | Damaged 0.5; worn 0.75; sound 1; actually exceptional 1.25 | | Urgency | Forced 0.75; normal 1; real patient auction 1.10 | Apply each factual factor once. An already applied Degraded half-value rule is not halved again as “damaged”; make the duplicate factor 1. Preparation with no price effect does not make material exceptional. A Gate Seal needs actual valid evidence. A patient auction needs its real appointment/buyer and waiting time. A disputed-provenance discount grants no right to sell another owner's property. **True artifacts.** Use the actual artifact formula and profile, with separately stated Base Function Value and Gate Tier Multiplier or a genuine finite buyer quote. Missing inputs mean *unvalued*, not zero or infinite price. No ordinary sword or crafted Masterwork acquires artifact multipliers by being recovered from the dungeon. Record gross and each deduction separately. A negative net estimate exposes a possible liability; it is not a compulsory purchase, debt or negative payment to a seller.

### FL-21 — One settlement ledger Keep exact fractions of copper until each actual final payment. Use 1 sp = 10 cp, 1 gp = 100 cp and 1 pp = 1,000 cp. Where accepted, retain 1 Mithril Mark = 500 cp, Embermark = 2 sp, Soulshard = 1 gp and Tidesilver = 1 sp. Verdant Leaf and otherwise unvalued currency have no invented universal conversion. Names do not establish currency origins. Round a final purchase, tax or fee payable **up** to copper once; round a final sale receipt **down** once. A coherent homogeneous sale bill is one receipt. Distinct real contracts can have separate final rounding; individual factors or components are not new transactions merely to change rounding. Displayed decimals never replace the exact value. For each entry, record transaction ID, payer/payee, currency, goods/quantity or service, agreement/authority, exact quote, actual rounded payment, timestamp, status and related prior payment. Quoted, reserved, paid, owed, refunded and lawfully written off are different states. A price quote spends nothing. Apply deposits to their agreed bill. Insurance is an inflow, not sold cargo. For the default Loop net-share sponsor agreement: `SponsorBase = max(0, G − T − RQ)` `SponsorShare = contracted percentage × SponsorBase, rounded once as payment` `NetExpedition = G − T − RQ − SponsorShare` G is actual sale receipts, T the direct Haven taxes on them, and RQ the episode's actual mandatory rescue/quarantine expenses. Count RQ once whether paid earlier or now. This sponsor base is before personal wages and discretionary purchases. A signed gross-share or priority-lien agreement instead uses its own declared terms. True profit includes actual episode inflows less every distinct actual episode cost once: shares, wages, consumed/replaced supplies, operating fuel, repair, interest and other agreed costs. Show capital purchases and borrowed principal separately. Loans and principal repayment are financing, and selling existing personal capital is not earned cargo. Cash allocated to next-expedition reserves is a further allocation, not automatically the same as profit. Report the charter's gross cargo target, net expedition target and true-profit/distributable-after-reserves target, stating whether the comparison is an appraisal or a realized sale. Appraised value does not pay wages. Keep insufficiently funded obligations owed; do not invent negative inventory, a compulsory new loan or unlimited sponsor funds. Allocations cannot exceed actual available money.

### FL-25 — Coins, unlawful operations, labor and rescue Track each coin's denomination, composition, count/weight, custody and actual mint acceptance. Declare the assay method and suspected defect before the roll; do not make a generic and specific test for the same uncertainty or switch to the easier one after failure. | Generic bulk assay | DC | |---|---:| | Obvious defect | 10 | | Mixed/clipped coin | 13 | | Plated/adulterated coin | 16 | | Expert false mint | 19 | | Specific Core method/defect | DC | Preserved value range | |---|---:|---| | Trace shaving, 1–3% | 12 | 95–99% face | | Light shaving, 4–8% | 14 | 85–95% face | | Heavy shaving, 9–15% | 16 | 70–85% face | | Ruined shaving, 16–30%, once weighed | 10 | 40–70% face | | Washed/plated, without cutting or magic | 18 | 5–25% recoverable value | One ordinary assay work unit handles up to 100 coins or 10 lb, whichever limit is reached first, in 30 active minutes. Keep materially different variants identified. Use INT (Investigation) or the relevant actual proficient tool once. An applicable functioning jeweler's-scale, touchstone, milled-edge or merchant-test-kit method can supply its source proficiency contribution to that assay, not a second proficiency bonus, general training or supernatural detection. Destructive testing spends the actual sample. Routine documented weighing needs no new roll. Failure leaves uncertainty. Only a declared false-assessment stake can give a fallible critical-failure report; no die changes metal. New evidence or a genuinely different test can justify more work and another roll. Changing the appraiser alone cannot. KEEP ordinary assay fees at 1% of the face value of the actual accepted assay bill, minimum 1 gp for that real service, and remint fees at 2% of the recovered legitimate metal value accepted for actual reminting. A combined commissioned assay bill receives its minimum once, not per coin, variant or thirty-minute stage; services not incurred create no fee, and an already-owned private testing toolkit creates no fictional desk fee to its owner. KEEP the Loop greater-of rule for a holder lawfully established to be knowing, not a 10% cap. NEW explicit total-payment and fee allocation: let F be the confirmed false lot's face value, A the actual assay fee, R the actual remint fee, and S=A+R for the same assessed lot/bill; the total monetary liability is P=max(0.10×F,S), allocated to service fees S and an additional criminal fine of P−S=max(0,0.10×F−S). Do not charge P plus those fees or levy another 10% fine on top. Compute on exact amounts under FL-21/EC-10's existing final-transaction copper rounding; allocating the total between fees and fine does not itself create extra transactions. Credit actual prior payments and fees already withheld from returned legitimate metal once against the same liability, leaving only its unpaid balance. Confirmed counterfeit coin or plated false currency is seized in full only through actual lawful authority; seizure is neither a fee nor a payment credit. Genuine coins and legitimate metal remain separately identified and are returned with actual fee deductions accounted for once. An innocent holder with documented provenance pays no criminal fine; absent a lawful knowing-holder finding, this rule imposes no criminal fine. Suspicion, ancestry, a failed die or missing documentation alone does not establish knowledge. Assessment, collection and custody require actual authorized actors; an unpaid amount remains an obligation, not automatic borrowing or remote confiscation. Cutting/reminting takes the provider's actual work and links consumed/replaced coin identities to real metal/output quantities without duplication. Unlawful trade still needs real contacts, agreed terms, actual cargo movement, any real concealment/document act and actual payment. Resolve only stages that exist as separate uncertainties. A deal does not create forged authority, a new skill or a free Scribing recipe. Underways Heat is 0–6 for the actual operation/institution pursuit history. A triggering act adds its highest applicable category once: petty illicit 1, restricted 2, strategic theft/smuggling 3, trafficking/forbidden 4. At each completed 24-hour Haven interval with an active operation, roll once; d6 at or below Heat triggers the declared enforcement complication. Heat 0 has none. Faction reporting does not add a second roll. An actual accepted bribe of 10% of the agreed lot value reduces Heat by 1, or 25% by 2, spending the payment once. An active operation's Heat cannot fall below 1; no bribe is paid at 0. Refusal or unsuccessful negotiation grants no reduction. Renaming/repacking an operation does not reset evidence, Heat or unresolved legal consequences. Enforcement requires actual actors, authority and means, not remote automatic seizure. People remain actors with factual and asserted legal status recorded separately: Free, Contracted, Debt-Bound, Penal, Enslaved, Rescued/Liberated or Disputed. A label creates no ownership, restraint or immunity. Use actual body weight, equipment and reviewed casualty Load: Tiny 1.5, Small 3, Medium 6, Large 12; larger unsupported bodies require their profile. Petrification multiplies body pounds by 10, not casualty Load. All melded and external passenger equipment burdens an outside carrier. Voluntary passengers use their actual seats/custody facts, not captive ownership. Ordinary lawful wages are 1 gp/day unskilled, 3 gp skilled or 10 gp specialist; dangerous expedition work doubles them unless the named service or real contract supplies its own rate. Do not charge both. A wage day buys at most two eight-hour work Watches and a protected Rest opportunity. Extra risky/emergency duty requires actual agreement and its costs/Rest Debt. A lawful debt bond records principal, credited wages and agreed simple interest no greater than 10% per literal Opening; no hidden compounding or automatic debt. Coercion, kidnapping, fraud or unlawful confinement cannot demand an invented buyout. An actual trafficking investigation uses an Evidence Clock 0–4. A concrete accessible lead takes one active hour and the appropriate Investigation/relevant-skill task at declared DC/stakes. Success adds 1, Critical Success 2, capped at 4; repeated evidence adds nothing. At 4, seek a real authorized warrant/hearing or plan a genuine rescue/raid. The clock does not conjure police, prove a false report or resolve combat. Guards, restraints and escape routes are actual scene facts. Consent-based adult services remain distinct from trafficking, with the table's boundaries controlling.

### SO-01 — Ask for a concrete outcome State what your character wants and how they try to obtain it. You can describe the approach in ordinary words; you do not need to perform a voice, accent or persuasive speech. Before a consequential check, establish this scene frame: | Field | What to establish | |---|---| | Want | The specific change each side wants before the scene ends | | Leverage | The offer, evidence, threat or withholding each side can actually use | | Limit | What the decision-maker cannot or will not concede under current conditions | | Clock | The real deadline and time needed for this exchange | | Witness | Who can perceive the exchange or later receive a report | Identify the people involved, the resource or information requested, its owner/controller, and who can authorize the concession. A person may possess a key without permission to sell the building. A clerk may permit supervised viewing without permission to give away the record. The Director states the obtainable success and its terms, failure, any optional costly alternative, any available extra on Critical Success, and any extra consequence on Critical Failure. Agree the approach, ability/skill, resolution method, difficulty, duration and costs before committing the work and rolling. The Director can preserve secrets while explaining an observable obstacle or that this request cannot currently succeed. A promised ordinary Success cannot secretly require Critical Success or acquire a new price after the die. If willingness, authority and prerequisites already settle a routine request, record the agreement and carry it out without a check. If the requested outcome is impossible or presently unavailable, no check can create it. You may seek a different feasible outcome. Roll when a meaningful, possible uncertainty remains. Close the approach when its agreement, refusal or interruption is recorded. Later performance can still be pending. A new request follows the changed-circumstances rules below.

### SO-02 — Resolve the declared uncertainty Choose the procedure before seeing any dice. A social concession or bounded inference normally uses a task against a fixed DC. Two actors making genuinely opposed attempts can use opposed totals. An explicit feature using a saving throw or passive Insight keeps its own procedure. These are new ordinary references where no more specific source supplies the DC: | DC | Negotiable concession | |---:|---| | 10 | Plausible, modest and within the person's authority | | 13 | The person has a substantial reservation | | 16 | Difficult, but genuinely negotiable | | 19 | Exceptional leverage for an actually possible outcome | Do not add a general route-tier or standing modifier to these DCs. Use only adjustments an applicable rule actually grants. For a fixed task, compare the total with the DC: at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC−10 is Critical Failure; the remaining totals below DC are Failure. Then a natural 20 improves one degree and a natural 1 worsens one, bounded at the ends. An impossible action does not acquire a roll or a fabricated failure margin. | Final degree | Result | |---|---| | Critical Success | The promised success on its stated terms, plus only the declared available extra | | Success | The promised success on its stated terms | | Failure | The declared refusal/failure; a costly alternative exists only if offered beforehand and feasible | | Critical Failure | That failure plus only the declared actual extra consequence; a costly alternative exists only if expressly offered for this branch | An optional costly agreement is separate from the failed check. Accept its stated terms if willing and able, or decline and keep the unspent payment along with the refusal. Accepting needs no new roll merely to enact a feasible offer. Its performance still takes time, and the original roll remains failed. No outcome degree automatically supplies obedience, truth, standing, consent or resources. For opposed checks, compare the two declared final totals: higher wins; a tie leaves the existing situation unchanged. Task degree shifts for natural 1/20 do not apply, and there is no general opposed critical reward. Ordinary saves remain binary under Core. Apply an operative source's reroll only in its exact window and with its exact replacement rule.

### SO-06 — Keep one clock and a working channel Everyone participates on the same fictional clock. A ten-minute negotiation involving four people normally advances ten minutes, provided their actual exchanges fit that time. A person's contribution can occupy that interval without adding another ten minutes to the world. Declare these new ordinary time references before work: | Exchange | Actual time | |---|---| | Short request and answer | 1 minute | | Negotiated concession or evidence presentation | 10 minutes | | Formal complex negotiation/hearing | Its scheduled time; an ordinary disputed Haven hearing is 2 hours | Simple routine consent can be immediate within real brief communication. These references do not replace a printed Action, casting time, five-exchange limit or other specific procedure. Add time for actual extra exchanges or delays, not for how quickly a player speaks at the table. In initiative, each creature has at most six seconds of aggregate free ordinary speech/signs per numbered round. Replies, warnings and extra turns share it. Each additional six-second segment requires an available Action on a legal turn or an actual off-turn permission. Communication does not create an interruption, Reaction or additional Action. Use the fulfilled language rules for ten-minute rehearsal of up to six simple cues and each cue's actual hands, sight and distance. An interpreter first receives a comprehensible message, then conveys it through a channel the next person can receive. A three-second warning followed by a three-second rendition arrives at the second listener at six seconds. A ten-minute original speech plus its rendition needs time for both; relays do not happen instantly. Late information cannot backdate a decision, modifier, consent or saving-throw requirement. An interpreter does not supply a caster's verbal component, new fluency, a mental link, the meaning of an unknown proper name or proof the message is true. Use each participant's actual language, mode and script knowledge. A closed soundproof compartment cannot receive an oral instruction through a high check. Deafened does not itself prevent speaking or verbal components. Silenced prevents ordinary deliberate speech and actual verbal components, Chants and command words, while separately legal signs, thoughts or mental effects retain their own rules. An effect ending does not remove another overlapping prohibition. Form-specific limits and exact Oracle/Paladin exceptions remain in force. Player explanations and accessibility accommodations cost no fictional Action and produce no fictional speech or component.

currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### TR-01 — Choose an actual mount Use the complete [transport catalogue](TRANSPORT_CATALOGUE_CANDIDATE.md) for Camel, Donkey or mule, Elephant, Draft horse, Riding horse, War horse, Mastiff, Pony and Warhound. Each is a separate profile. “Donkey or mule” means one chosen individual. The printed price, walking Speed and carrying pounds are retained. The additional body size, mass, abilities, defenses, HP, Hit Dice, attack, training, nutrition, draw rating and Load cap are explicit new provisional game values. A carrying rating does not determine Strength or make a template a record of the particular animal being sold. Use the profile's natural AC, which already includes its Dexterity, and its fixed maximum HP. Record the individual's current HP, remaining Hit Dice, Wounds, conditions, injuries and training. Saves use its ability modifier without an added save proficiency unless an actual source grants it. Ordinary senses do not grant darkvision or automatic detection. These profiles supply no class levels, RP, spellcasting, special immunity or class features. An independent animal's listed attack costs its Action and makes one attack using that profile's bonus, reach and damage. Core attack criticals apply. It has no automatic charge damage, knockdown or Multiattack, and the rider receives no extra attack. A controlled ridden mount instead uses the restricted Action choices below. Large mounts occupy a 10-foot square, Medium mounts a 5-foot square, and the new Huge Elephant a 15-foot square. A saddle admits one physically compatible rider at least one size smaller. A Medium character cannot ride a Medium Pony merely because their weight is low. Count the rider, all equipment, tack, containers and contents against both the mount's pounds and Load limits. Its separate harness draw rating is not extra back capacity. A positive carried burden at or above half either profile limit applies the one Burdened penalty: Speed −10 feet and disadvantage to climbing, swimming or moving silently. Do not apply it twice because both measures qualify. Routine carriage must fit both full limits and the actual body/seat geometry. A registered ordinary expedition mount is, by this new default, a significant creature using Core Wounds, dying and death saves. Establish that status before the encounter. An actual Ranger Beast bond instead follows its own HP-only, immediate-death lifecycle. No repair, stable fee, new template or replacement purchase revives a dead individual.

### TR-02 — Control and training A physically compatible, trained and willing mount can be controlled. An intelligent or untrained independent mount keeps its own agency. Ownership, restraint and payment do not establish willingness or training. A conscious, nonincapacitated seated rider can direct intended movement and choose the controlled mount's one allowed Action: **Dash, Disengage or Dodge**. Use an actual trained audible or tactile channel. An audible cue shares the language rules' speech allowance. Reins require an available hand; a trained seat/leg cue works only if that individual knows it and the current seat permits it. Ordinary riding direction adds no separate Bonus Action. It does not issue a class companion command, authorize an attack or transfer rider bonuses to the animal. A controlled mount with its own regular turn counts toward the controller's existing limit of two commanded independent-turn combat-capable subordinates. The controller's own character is separate. A source-bound companion with only an attached phase retains its own command and offensive budgets; calling it a mount does not give it a full turn. Additional pack animals can be led outside combat through real handling, but do not give a third controlled combat turn. There is no automatic animal swarm. An independent NPC acting as a party character counts toward the twelve-character roster. A merely ridden animal does not occupy a member seat, although its actions, cargo, provisions and history still matter. Independent animals are directed by their real agency, not treated as free player attack orders. Recheck control when the mount acts. If the rider is no longer seated or able to cue it, the channel fails, or the mount is unable or unwilling, an unexecuted riding cue cannot compel it. If able, it defensively Dodges and stays still or moves only to an immediately safer available space, chosen through its actual agency. Its existing turn and spent budgets do not reset. An executed cue is not undone. A legitimate trained noncombat lead/follow cue can continue only while its actual conditions and handler remain available. **New ordinary training course.** A genuinely tame, willing animal can learn one named riding or harness function through 40 active hours, at most four credited training hours per animal per day. The instructor needs Animal Handling proficiency, a suitable safe space, fitting tack and a usable conditioning method. Credit complete 15-minute phases. An interruption loses unfinished prospective phase credit; actual time, feed and fees remain spent. The full-course tuition reference is 5 gp, unless an actual voluntary or paid agreement differs. Completion requires the real course and demonstrated safe routine behavior. It grants only the practiced function, without an obedience spell, rider proficiency or Ranger bond. A documented already-trained animal needs no repeat course. Wildness or unwillingness cannot be cured by depositing hours. A war-named purchase includes combat habituation only if its actual contract and behavior establish it. Feed, water, tack and stabling are separate unless genuinely included.

### TR-03 — One complete mount turn At initiative registration, a controlled mount shares its rider's initiative value and takes one complete regular turn immediately **after** the rider's complete regular turn. Their movement and Actions do not interleave. You cannot move the mount twenty feet, insert a free rider attack segment, then finish the mount's movement. You may Ready a permitted Action through the normal procedure, paying your Action and later Reaction, with its actual trigger, components and duration. This creates no free attack. An independent mount keeps its own initiative and choices. The mount has its own regular-start/end markers, movement, normal Action and applicable Reaction budget. Its controlled Actions remain Dash, Disengage and Dodge. Control grants no offensive Reaction or opportunity attack; a specific defensive Reaction works only if actually available. It makes its own death saves when its lifecycle requires them. A rider's extra turn does not create another mount turn, start, recharge or condition tick. Each physical actor receives at most one scheduled regular turn per numbered round. Mounting, dismounting or changing controllers retains its spent budgets and original allocated slot for that round. A new valid controlled relation takes its new rider-linked position beginning next round. This round, use the existing unspent slot if any; never replay a taken one. A mount entering mid-round uses a legal not-yet-passed insertion under the combat-entry rules, or starts next round. It does not replay the new rider's earlier slot. Changing to independent behavior also grants no second turn. Separate rider and mount effects still expire at their own stated markers even when initiative values match.

### TR-04 — Mounting, dismounting and losing the seat An ordinary mount or voluntary dismount costs half your current walking Speed, rounded down in feet, from your remaining regular movement. A positive Speed whose half is below one instead costs one foot. Speed 0 does not permit it. You may perform at most one mount **or** dismount operation per regular turn; an extra turn supplies no additional operation through this rule. The cost is movement, not a Bonus Action or free object interaction. Start within five feet of the accessible seat at a reachable height, with a stable approach, one usable supporting hand and a physically fitting destination. A high Elephant saddle needs actual steps, help or a legal route to reach it; an exotic saddle does not lift you. If Prone, first stand using the real cost or use another valid assisted procedure. Mounting does not remove Prone. To dismount, choose a visible, free adjacent space within five feet of the relevant body boundary at a reachable level. A wall, another creature, an inadequate gap or an unpaid fall is not a legal destination. Insufficient remaining movement or an inaccessible seat prevents the ordinary operation. A specific acquired feature overrides only its actual clause. The animal's remaining movement and Actions stay unchanged. When one resolved source event moves a seated rider's mount against its will **or** knocks it Prone, the rider makes one DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. If that same event does both, make one save. Distinct events can each trigger a save. This is a binary Core save with no generic natural 1/20 degree shifts. On failure, leave the seat and land Prone in the first legal adjacent space from your recorded dismount preference, or the Director's neutral accessible ordering. Resolve actual height and falling under the falling rules; unseating adds no fixed damage by itself. On success, retain the seat only if support remains physically possible. A Prone mount does not automatically make its successful rider Prone, but its awkward body and blocked movement still matter. A rider independently made Prone gains that condition without another seat save. Voluntary ordinary travel alone causes no save. If an exact effect ejects you regardless of a save, use that effect and the actual landing. Impossible support or landing resolves through the real fall/entrapment situation, never placement inside a wall.

### TR-05 — Position, areas and opportunity attacks Record the rider's actual saddle point or fitting five-foot subspace on the mount before movement. Attacks, reach, line of effect and area exposure use that position, not every edge of an Elephant's footprint. Moving to another accessible seat position takes your own real movement, path and support. Rider and mount remain two creatures with separate AC, HP, conditions and resources. An area can affect both if it actually includes each; resolve separate saves and damage histories. Riding grants no automatic cover, shared HP or immunity. Actual barriers and body geometry can supply cover under the normal rules. When the mount's own voluntary movement provokes a legal opportunity attack, the reactor may choose the mount **or** rider. The chosen target must actually be visible and within legal reach/line at the departure edge. Spend one available Reaction for one permitted ordinary attack before completing that departure step. One provoking move is not an attack on each creature, and a distant rider's seat does not become reachable merely because the mount is adjacent. The mount's Disengage prevents the opportunity provoked by its movement, including this rider-or-mount choice. The rider's own Disengage protects the rider's own voluntary movement; it does not give the mount Disengage. Your own movement around the seat or while dismounting uses your own opportunity-attack rules. Forced displacement or teleportation does not provoke a generic movement opportunity attack, although an actual seat-save trigger or other specific effect may apply. An attack against the mount does not automatically damage or unseat its rider; its actual consequence must trigger that result. Vehicle carriage does not use this living-mount exception. Passive displacement of vehicle occupants gives no generic opportunity attack without a specific source. Moving pullers can provoke for themselves, without granting an attack through a wall against a distant passenger.

### TR-06 — Movement belongs to the actor who performs it Riding changes your position, but it does not automatically spend your movement, perform your leap, count as your flight or charge, deal your weapon damage or activate a class feature. Track who moves under their own power, who is carried, the path, forced or teleport displacement, the budget spent, and whose turn it is. A rule asking whether someone is within a distance still uses actual positions. Cavalry and Mounted Combatant remain separate pending feats. Ordinary riding grants neither their attack advantages nor Cavalry's +10 mount Speed. Their different prerequisites and attack scopes are not merged or assumed to stack. Dragoon Momentum keeps its actual engine: genuine self-powered movement of at least 15 feet toward a tactical destination on the Dragoon's regular turn supplies its one movement gain; a qualifying personal weapon-damage event supplies the other default gain. All gains and refunds remain capped at two per round. Being carried, forced movement, teleportation, movement in place, allies, summons or another actor's hit does not qualify. A mount's leap is not the Dragoon's paid leap technique. **New narrow transport interpretation:** the Dragoon's separate requirement to move at least twenty feet on its turn before a Weave cast counts actual voluntary self-propelled path, including a legitimately paid source leap. It excludes carriage, forced movement and teleportation. Keep the actual before-cast window and the Dissonance reduction of one, minimum zero. It grants no RP discount or additional Momentum. Other class, oath, ancestry, spell and companion movement rules retain their exact acquired effects. This interpretation does not rewrite every distance condition or prohibit an actual feature expressly benefiting passive carriage.

### TR-13 — One route rate, with real transfers Route quality, mapping knowledge and Risk are separate. A well-mapped collapsed bridge remains physically collapsed. | Physical route quality | Travel-time multiplier | |---|---:| | Secured | 0.75 | | Known | 1 | | Contested | 1.25 | | Collapsed | 1.50 | For the ordinary route-work tranche, use: `480 active minutes × physical quality × (3 ÷ limiting convoy mph)` An explicit route mode/duration can replace that reference only through its actual rule. The forced Unknown march's nominal 480-minute attempt uses this same normalization, not an additional eight hours or an unadjusted fast pace. Do not award both a route-progress result and a second distance from those same hours. For these creatures, ordinary travel mph is current otherwise-legal walking Speed divided by ten, after applicable burden, injury and environmental modifiers. Apply the reviewed Strain-5 half-travel penalty once. Watercraft use the actual available propulsion/current ground rate. The convoy is limited by its slowest necessary moving member, puller or carrier. A passenger contributes the carrier's movement, not their own Speed. An essential stopped, overloaded or unavailable carrier stops convoy progress until a real transfer, repair or route change. Leaving it behind is an actual split or abandonment. A Speed change affects only the remaining route work; preserve completed distance/fractional progress. The source Secured −1 and Contested +1 threat modifiers adjust effective Pressure for the **single ordinary travel complication check**, clamped 0–6. They do not change stored Pressure or cause another roll. Collapsed adds the actual physical obstacle's +3 difficulty where that obstacle exists. The extraction checkpoint's specific secured −2/pursuit/exposure formula remains separate; do not add a second route modifier for the same secured condition. Core's Known one-Load, Contested 10% and Collapsed 20%-or-reroute losses are possible predeclared stakes, not automatic additional penalties on a complication or failed extraction check. Choose the consequence model beforehand. A declared percentage uses the current at-risk manifest and actual eligible lots/portions in a predeclared priority, with permitted unit rounding. Never delete part of a person or indivisible object to satisfy the fraction. Unachievable remainder is not banked. Secured's “none” removes that routine table-loss rider, not actual separate danger. Changing mount, cart or ship takes a real transfer interval with receivers, crew and route ready. Retain Extraction Class, title, custody, material age, identity and closed claims. A transport-mode rename does not cross a checkpoint again. A genuinely new border, exit or handover can be its own declared finite checkpoint.

currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### FL-02 — Members, teams and offices An Expedition has at most **12 member characters**, including recruited NPCs and hirelings assigned independent Expedition jobs. Small Expeditions can use fewer teams and undertake feasible solo tasks. The following sizes are recommendations, not entry requirements. | Team | Suggested members | Work | |---|---:|---| | Combat | 4–6 | Threats, battles and immediate protection | | Reconnaissance | 1–3 | Scouting and mapping | | Research | 1–3 | Study and identification | | Resource | 2–4 | Gathering, crafting and harvesting | | Support | 1–3 | Camp, care, repair and transport | Appoint the five source offices: **Expedition Leader**, **Quartermaster**, **Routekeeper**, **Surgeon**, and **Claimant of Record**. The Leader represents the company and records tied organizational decisions; the Quartermaster tracks provisions, Load, cargo priority, wages and losses; the Routekeeper maintains the map; the Surgeon directs Wound treatment and casualty transport; the Claimant of Record maintains provenance, contracts and ownership documents. One person can hold several offices. An office grants no skill, extra Action or power over another player's consent or another owner's property. Before work, record each member's primary activity or Rest, location, intended result, lead and assistants, and actual start/end times. Short tasks may follow one another. A person cannot perform incompatible activities during the same seconds. For a generic expedition task, up to three trained assistants who provide meaningful help each add +1. Exact crafting, harvesting, preservation, social and companion procedures use their own assistance rules instead. Porters, bearers, guards and drivers contracted as members occupy roster seats. A public ship or caravan's external crew stays on its own service record and is not additional party labor or automatic combat support. Animals and source-bound noncharacter companions/devices do not occupy character seats; an intelligent creature recruited as an autonomous expedition character does. Larger forces use distinct cooperating Expeditions with real communication, shared finite resources and the same world clock.

### TR-02 — Control and training A physically compatible, trained and willing mount can be controlled. An intelligent or untrained independent mount keeps its own agency. Ownership, restraint and payment do not establish willingness or training. A conscious, nonincapacitated seated rider can direct intended movement and choose the controlled mount's one allowed Action: **Dash, Disengage or Dodge**. Use an actual trained audible or tactile channel. An audible cue shares the language rules' speech allowance. Reins require an available hand; a trained seat/leg cue works only if that individual knows it and the current seat permits it. Ordinary riding direction adds no separate Bonus Action. It does not issue a class companion command, authorize an attack or transfer rider bonuses to the animal. A controlled mount with its own regular turn counts toward the controller's existing limit of two commanded independent-turn combat-capable subordinates. The controller's own character is separate. A source-bound companion with only an attached phase retains its own command and offensive budgets; calling it a mount does not give it a full turn. Additional pack animals can be led outside combat through real handling, but do not give a third controlled combat turn. There is no automatic animal swarm. An independent NPC acting as a party character counts toward the twelve-character roster. A merely ridden animal does not occupy a member seat, although its actions, cargo, provisions and history still matter. Independent animals are directed by their real agency, not treated as free player attack orders. Recheck control when the mount acts. If the rider is no longer seated or able to cue it, the channel fails, or the mount is unable or unwilling, an unexecuted riding cue cannot compel it. If able, it defensively Dodges and stays still or moves only to an immediately safer available space, chosen through its actual agency. Its existing turn and spent budgets do not reset. An executed cue is not undone. A legitimate trained noncombat lead/follow cue can continue only while its actual conditions and handler remain available. **New ordinary training course.** A genuinely tame, willing animal can learn one named riding or harness function through 40 active hours, at most four credited training hours per animal per day. The instructor needs Animal Handling proficiency, a suitable safe space, fitting tack and a usable conditioning method. Credit complete 15-minute phases. An interruption loses unfinished prospective phase credit; actual time, feed and fees remain spent. The full-course tuition reference is 5 gp, unless an actual voluntary or paid agreement differs. Completion requires the real course and demonstrated safe routine behavior. It grants only the practiced function, without an obedience spell, rider proficiency or Ranger bond. A documented already-trained animal needs no repeat course. Wildness or unwillingness cannot be cured by depositing hours. A war-named purchase includes combat habituation only if its actual contract and behavior establish it. Feed, water, tack and stabling are separate unless genuinely included.

### TR-03 — One complete mount turn At initiative registration, a controlled mount shares its rider's initiative value and takes one complete regular turn immediately **after** the rider's complete regular turn. Their movement and Actions do not interleave. You cannot move the mount twenty feet, insert a free rider attack segment, then finish the mount's movement. You may Ready a permitted Action through the normal procedure, paying your Action and later Reaction, with its actual trigger, components and duration. This creates no free attack. An independent mount keeps its own initiative and choices. The mount has its own regular-start/end markers, movement, normal Action and applicable Reaction budget. Its controlled Actions remain Dash, Disengage and Dodge. Control grants no offensive Reaction or opportunity attack; a specific defensive Reaction works only if actually available. It makes its own death saves when its lifecycle requires them. A rider's extra turn does not create another mount turn, start, recharge or condition tick. Each physical actor receives at most one scheduled regular turn per numbered round. Mounting, dismounting or changing controllers retains its spent budgets and original allocated slot for that round. A new valid controlled relation takes its new rider-linked position beginning next round. This round, use the existing unspent slot if any; never replay a taken one. A mount entering mid-round uses a legal not-yet-passed insertion under the combat-entry rules, or starts next round. It does not replay the new rider's earlier slot. Changing to independent behavior also grants no second turn. Separate rider and mount effects still expire at their own stated markers even when initiative values match.

### TR-10 — Porters, bearers and hired pack animals | Service | Contracted customer cargo | Base daily price | |---|---:|---:| | Porter | 2 Load | 2 sp, plus agreed danger pay | | Skilled bearer | 3 Load | 1 gp | | Pack-animal hire | 6 Load | 5 sp, plus feed | These are customer allowances, not a biological capacity increase. Name the actual worker or animal and check their own gear plus the promised cargo against their real pounds, Load, shape, fatigue and terrain limits. A stronger porter does not automatically owe more work; extra carriage needs a feasible amended agreement. Core's porter safe 2/maximum 4 and pack-animal safe 6/maximum 10 Load describe emergency offer limits. Extra loads require an expressly accepted feasible operation, with actual burden/drag penalties and risk. They never override the individual's body limits or grant free overflow. A bought Camel, mule or other mount keeps its own complete profile. A hired six-Load service must provide one identified suitable trained animal; it is not an interchangeable invisible body. Record the operator separately. Hire does not include a human handler, saddle, water, feed or stabling unless the real agreement includes them. Do not charge both purchase and hire for the same delivered ownership interest. Late-return or loss liability must be agreed, not invented from the market price. A service day is 24 elapsed hours of custody with at most two eight-hour assigned work Watches and actual Rest. Charge a started day once under the agreement; loading again or crossing a Haven gate does not restart the bill. The named service rate takes precedence over generic wages. Accepted dangerous duty defaults to twice that rate once, unless a different prospective agreement applies. Work already performed earns its agreed wage even when a task fails; refunds and liability follow the actual contract. People hired into ordinary expedition jobs count toward the twelve-member roster. A public carrier's external crew stays on its service roster and supplies no free party jobs. Record consent, duties, knowledge, communication, pay, supplies, HP, Strain, rest, custody and departure. A wounded, exhausted or absent provider requires a real replacement and transfer; treating someone as cargo does not compel obedience.

currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### FL-03 — One clock, work and rest The campaign uses one elapsed clock. A Watch is eight hours; a day contains Morning, Afternoon and Evening Watches. Combat rounds, rests, travel, treatment and work occupy their actual time within that clock. Completing a task does not add a second Watch. Entering Haven, changing teams or starting initiative does not reset elapsed time. A generic Watch task needs **480 active minutes** before its completion check. Feasible unfinished work can continue in another Watch, without a proportional completion reward. Exact recipes, uninterrupted training, treatment, rest and spells keep their own interruption rules. Guarding, travelling, casting, directing, interpreting, assisting or working cannot also count as incompatible rest. Passive carriage qualifies for rest only when a genuinely suitable safe berth and the actual rest requirements are satisfied. Plan at most two active work Watches and one Rest Watch per person each day. Evening is the default Rest slot; change it prospectively before that day's first assignment. Voluntary extra noncrafting travel or guard duty can replace Rest and incur its real costs and Rest Debt. This supplies no third crafting, training, research or harvesting Watch. Emergencies still consume time and interrupt the activity underway. Missing a scheduled Rest creates **Rest Debt**. If an emergency interrupts Rest, the debt opens after that emergency ends; otherwise it opens when the missed Rest Watch ends. Complete a qualifying safe eight-hour Rest by the end of the second following canonical Watch. If the debt remains unpaid at that deadline, gain 1 Strain once for that due event and keep owing the Rest. Missing another scheduled Rest while indebted gives 1 Strain and resets the deadline. There is no automatic additional Strain every second or every Watch merely because the same debt remains. A safe eight-hour Rest clears the debt even when you cannot receive another Long Rest's benefits. Keep the separate limits: one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours, two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests, the existing four-hour Morale Rest, and 24-hour Haven care. Trance reduces sleep, not the eight-hour Long-Rest requirement. Use the actual Strain and recovery chapter for what can be removed.

### FL-18 — Durability, old Integrity records and repair Use actual structural HP for modeled equipment, fixtures and transport bodies. The old 0–3 Integrity track is not another damage pool, and its old Integrity-1 penalty does not automatically apply to a functioning positive-HP item. Keep actual grade, quality, flaws, constituents and custody. Living mounts use living HP and conditions, not structural repair. At zero structural HP, an object is Broken under the [equipment rules](../EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md). It still exists with mass, occupied space and physical drawbacks until actually removed or repaired. A missing wheel or other true primary constituent can make a vehicle incomplete even with positive aggregate HP. Inventing a cheap “pin” target does not disable a whole structure. Ordinary self-repair requires a relevant trained toolkit and real compatible material worth **25% of the item's proper size/grade baseline**. Spend **max(1 hour, maximum structural HP ÷ 10 hours)** of active work and make the appropriate DC 10 tool task. Collapse Core degrees to success/failure: success restores maximum structural HP; failure spends time/materials and a new attempt needs fresh payment. A critical supplies no extra generic benefit. Repair at zero HP requires the recoverable main body. An eight-hour Repair Watch is eight hours of available work, not eight completions. A 300-HP mundane vessel needs 30 active hours under this profile. Magical recipe bodies retain their exact functional/Broken bridge, prices, primary identities and persistent flaws. Repair does not recreate missing items, passengers, doses, ammunition, burnt pages, fuel, charges, class gauges or a terminal dismantled source.

### TR-11 — The bound hauler and specialist services **Core transport hauler.** The retained reference is 500 gp plus fuel, with actual Tier-IV-or-higher availability, 20 normal Load and 30 emergency maximum. The new complete profile is a separate transport-only magical nonartifact machine. It is not a creature, summoned body, class companion, AEX automaton, recipe 507/670 or PC. It has no CR, mind, creature turn, attack, spell, RP, corpse/drop or class-command entitlement. Its empty 120 lb wheeled frame measures 5×3×4 feet with a 4×2×2-foot clear bed, AC 19 and 60 maximum structural HP. Normal payload is 200 lb/20 Load at Speed 30 feet/3 mph. Over either normal rating, emergency carriage is limited to 300 lb/30 Load at Speed 5 feet/0.5 mph. Shape, full supported gross weight and a clear firm route remain necessary; never exceed either emergency maximum. One real adjacent operator within five feet, with access to the controls and both manipulating hands, spends an Action for one drive event per numbered round, moving at most its current Speed over a feasible path. It cannot Dash, climb, fly, use stairs, act remotely or run an autonomous program. Another Action cannot buy another drive. Outside initiative the operator works continuously. Being aboard does not help if the controls are out of reach. This local mechanism is distinct from TI04's binding, channel and shared offensive-device budgets. **Fuel.** One actual compatible lamp-oil pint, reference 10 cp/1 lb, powers eight accumulated active propulsion hours. The reservoir holds one pint. Consume exact proportional fuel as it actually operates; pauses consume no propulsion fuel, while leaks/losses persist. Refilling a stationary machine takes one active minute, two hands and available oil. Purchase creates no free oil or flask. Oil already spent for propulsion cannot also light a lamp or remain unspent Supply. This power grants no transferable energy, RP, distillate or spellcasting. **Service.** At each forty accumulated moving hours, service is due before further propulsion. On the stationary serviceable mechanism, a qualified Vehicles (Land) or appropriate Tinker's-tools practitioner spends one active hour, suitable tools and one actual 1 gp/0.5 lb grease/fastener pack. Routine completed service needs no check. It clears only the due-service counter, restoring no HP, fuel or lost part. An interrupted service retains completed work but provides no completion until finished; it is not rest. A differently named AEX pack is not interchangeable without real compatible quantities. **Restoration.** This hauler's explicit new magical repair bridge uses actual compatible materials at a 125 gp reference and qualified Vehicles (Land)/Tinker's tools. Positive-HP functional repair takes six active hours at DC 10. HP-0 reconstruction takes eight active hours at DC 15 and requires the original primary frame, drive unit and controller. Use Core task degree shifts, collapsing to success/failure without extra critical effects. Success restores this body's maximum HP/function only. Failure spends work and materials. Subordinate wheels, straps and fasteners can be replaced with real stock; missing primary assemblies or terminal dismantling cannot be recreated by payment. Fuel, service history, ownership and closed claims do not reset. **Gate caravan.** The retained 100+ Load/10%-of-cargo-value reference is a real large service. Its quote must state a finite offered capacity of at least 100 Load, pounds and geometry, occupants, actual journey/route, staff, containers, custody, appraisal base, danger and schedule. Paying the fee does not cross a restricted Gate or move cargo. Staff do not become free expedition combat support. **Teleport extraction.** The reference is Tier×100 gp for each accepted Extraction Load. The new default rounds the accepted positive total upward to a whole Load once per commissioned bill, unless an actual finite source contract states another rule. Execution still needs a currently operative acquired effect with its full endpoints, range, person/object/mass/volume limits, consent, access, costs and containment. A price table supplies no spell or destination permission. Without that particular procedure/endpoint, that service is unavailable; ordinary transport remains usable.

### TR-14 — Recover living creatures; repair actual structures Living mounts use creature healing, HP, Hit Dice, Wounds, injuries, conditions, rest eligibility, nutrition and their actual lifecycle. Healing can end dying only as its procedure permits. Repair work, a quarter-price bill, insurance, stabling or buying another animal does not revive the dead individual. The ordinary significant-mount default remains distinct from a Ranger Beast's HP-only exception and finite creations. Actual remains use existing once-only harvest rules, not a resource yield invented from price or carrying capacity. Objects use structural HP and their real material/object defenses. They receive no creature Wounds, death saves or parallel duplicate Integrity penalties. For a positive-HP or genuinely reparable mundane HP-0 main body, trained appropriate-tool self-repair uses actual compatible materials at 25% of the applicable undamaged mundane body reference, DC 10, and active work of `max(1 hour, recorded maximum HP ÷ 10 hours)`. Apply Core task shifts with the upper two degrees as success and lower two as failure, without extra critical benefits. A 300-HP hull therefore takes thirty active hours, not one Watch or thirty independent restorations. The worker needs the actually appropriate carpenter, smith or vehicle tools and a workable supported/dry site. A complete qualified service quote at the source's 10%/15% price is alternative pricing, not another 25% material charge. Recipe-magical equipment keeps its own reviewed procedure; the Core hauler uses its specific new repair bridge above. Success restores the same body's HP to its existing permitted maximum/function. It does not recreate missing primary structure, restore cargo, fuel, charges, service credit, magical imprint, flaws or closed claims unless an actual rule expressly does so. Compatible subordinate parts use actual stock once; the profile's required original primary members must survive. Failure spends actual materials and work. Another permitted attempt requires new inputs, not a free reroll. Terminal dismantling is not merely HP 0. Custody, material age and source clocks continue during repair and storage. Drawn frames and the hauler at HP 0 are disabled and strand their real load. Unload, transfer, support or tow only through a feasible method. Occupants are not automatically damaged solely because structural HP reaches zero. **New afloat-hull emergency.** Without a specific different destruction source, a watercraft reaching HP 0 becomes disabled and starts one ten-minute flooding/evacuation deadline. At that deadline its wreck becomes submerged or stranded according to the real depth and support. It is not deleted, and occupants use actual escape, falling, swimming and drowning rules. Once per actual hull-breaking episode, two capable workers, at least one trained with carpenter's tools or Vehicles (Water), can spend five uninterrupted active minutes and real compatible patch/bracing supplies at 1% of the undamaged body reference, minimum 1 gp. The work must finish before the flooding deadline. Make the appropriate DC 15 tool task using Core shifts collapsed to success/failure. Success holds that same disabled hull afloat for sixty minutes from completion, without restoring HP or propulsion. Failure spends work/materials and leaves the original deadline. Repeating the label cannot reset the same rupture or bank more time. Real grounding, docking, towing or a hoist can support the still-present wreck for full repair. Rescue uses actual people, tools, locations, mass, Actions and time. It creates no lifeboat, fresh crew, stretcher, survivor or recovered property. Apply ordinary cargo rescue where appropriate and encounter procedures under actual threat. Insurance pays only an eligible recorded loss; it does not automatically repurchase inaccessible unique bodies.

currentExpeditionSections.fullSection: ### FL-03 — One clock, work and rest The campaign uses one elapsed clock. A Watch is eight hours; a day contains Morning, Afternoon and Evening Watches. Combat rounds, rests, travel, treatment and work occupy their actual time within that clock. Completing a task does not add a second Watch. Entering Haven, changing teams or starting initiative does not reset elapsed time. A generic Watch task needs **480 active minutes** before its completion check. Feasible unfinished work can continue in another Watch, without a proportional completion reward. Exact recipes, uninterrupted training, treatment, rest and spells keep their own interruption rules. Guarding, travelling, casting, directing, interpreting, assisting or working cannot also count as incompatible rest. Passive carriage qualifies for rest only when a genuinely suitable safe berth and the actual rest requirements are satisfied. Plan at most two active work Watches and one Rest Watch per person each day. Evening is the default Rest slot; change it prospectively before that day's first assignment. Voluntary extra noncrafting travel or guard duty can replace Rest and incur its real costs and Rest Debt. This supplies no third crafting, training, research or harvesting Watch. Emergencies still consume time and interrupt the activity underway. Missing a scheduled Rest creates **Rest Debt**. If an emergency interrupts Rest, the debt opens after that emergency ends; otherwise it opens when the missed Rest Watch ends. Complete a qualifying safe eight-hour Rest by the end of the second following canonical Watch. If the debt remains unpaid at that deadline, gain 1 Strain once for that due event and keep owing the Rest. Missing another scheduled Rest while indebted gives 1 Strain and resets the deadline. There is no automatic additional Strain every second or every Watch merely because the same debt remains. A safe eight-hour Rest clears the debt even when you cannot receive another Long Rest's benefits. Keep the separate limits: one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours, two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests, the existing four-hour Morale Rest, and 24-hour Haven care. Trance reduces sleep, not the eight-hour Long-Rest requirement. Use the actual Strain and recovery chapter for what can be removed.
